## Goals

-   Fit logistic and Poisson regression with `glm()`
-   Use `marginaleffects` to report effects on the response scale
-   Show that the chi-square test is a log-linear model

## Setup



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(tidyverse)
library(marginaleffects)
```
:::



## Binary data: logistic regression

Simulated seedling survival in sun vs. shade (60 seedlings each):



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
set.seed(11)
seedlings <- tibble(light = rep(c("Sun", "Shade"), each = 60)) |>
  mutate(light = factor(light, levels = c("Shade", "Sun")),
         survived = rbinom(n(), 1, ifelse(light == "Sun", 0.7, 0.4)))
```
:::

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
m_log <- glm(survived ~ light, family = binomial, data = seedlings)
summary(m_log)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

Call:
glm(formula = survived ~ light, family = binomial, data = seedlings)

Coefficients:
            Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
(Intercept)  -0.7691     0.2775  -2.771  0.00558 ** 
lightSun      2.5037     0.4558   5.493 3.95e-08 ***
---
Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1

(Dispersion parameter for binomial family taken to be 1)

    Null deviance: 163.01  on 119  degrees of freedom
Residual deviance: 125.64  on 118  degrees of freedom
AIC: 129.64

Number of Fisher Scoring iterations: 4
```


:::
:::



The `lightSun` coefficient is a **log odds ratio**. Few people can interpret that. Ask in the units of the data:



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
avg_predictions(m_log, by = "light")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

 light Estimate Pr(>|z|)    S 2.5 % 97.5 %
 Shade    0.317  0.00558  7.5 0.212  0.444
 Sun      0.850  < 0.001 19.2 0.736  0.920

Columns: rowid, light, estimate, p.value, s.value, conf.low, conf.high, rowid_dedup 
Type:  invlink(link) 
```


:::
:::

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
avg_comparisons(m_log, variables = "light")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

  Term    Contrast Estimate Std. Error    z Pr(>|z|)    S 2.5 % 97.5 %
 light Sun - Shade    0.533     0.0757 7.04   <0.001 39.0 0.385  0.682

Columns: term, contrast, estimate, std.error, statistic, p.value, s.value, conf.low, conf.high 
Type:  response 
```


:::
:::



The difference in survival probability is the effect size most biologists want. Ratios are available too:



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
avg_comparisons(m_log, variables = "light", comparison = "ratio")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

  Term    Contrast Estimate Std. Error    z Pr(>|z|)    S 2.5 % 97.5 %
 light Sun / Shade     2.68      0.529 5.07   <0.001 21.3  1.65   3.72

Columns: term, contrast, estimate, std.error, statistic, p.value, s.value, conf.low, conf.high 
Type:  response 
```


:::
:::

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
avg_comparisons(m_log, variables = "light", comparison = "lnor", transform = "exp")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

  Term                    Contrast Estimate Pr(>|z|)    S 2.5 % 97.5 %
 light ln(odds(Sun) / odds(Shade))     12.2   <0.001 24.6     5   29.9

Columns: term, contrast, estimate, p.value, s.value, conf.low, conf.high 
Type:  response 
```


:::
:::



::: callout-note
## Exercise 1

Which is more informative to report: the risk difference, the risk ratio, or the odds ratio? When might they tell very different stories?
:::

## A continuous predictor in a GLM

Add seedling height:



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
seedlings$height <- round(rnorm(nrow(seedlings), 10, 2), 1)
m_log2 <- glm(survived ~ light + height, family = binomial, data = seedlings)
```
:::

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
plot_predictions(m_log2, condition = c("height", "light")) +
  theme_minimal()
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![Predicted survival probability across height and light](week11-tutorial_files/figure-html/fig-logit-1.png){#fig-logit width=672}
:::
:::

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
avg_slopes(m_log2, variables = "height")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

   Term Estimate Std. Error     z Pr(>|z|)   S   2.5 %   97.5 %
 height   -0.038     0.0186 -2.05   0.0406 4.6 -0.0744 -0.00162

Columns: term, estimate, std.error, statistic, p.value, s.value, conf.low, conf.high 
Type:  response 
```


:::
:::



## Count data: Poisson regression

`InsectSprays`: insects surviving six insecticide sprays.



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
ggplot(InsectSprays, aes(spray, count)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  theme_minimal()
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](week11-tutorial_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-11-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
m_pois <- glm(count ~ spray, family = poisson, data = InsectSprays)
```
:::

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
avg_predictions(m_pois, by = "spray")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

 spray Estimate Pr(>|z|)     S 2.5 % 97.5 %
     A    14.50   <0.001 903.0 12.50  16.82
     B    15.33   <0.001 994.8 13.27  17.72
     C     2.08   <0.001  12.0  1.41   3.08
     D     4.92   <0.001 111.9  3.81   6.35
     E     3.50   <0.001  50.9  2.59   4.74
     F    16.67   <0.001   Inf 14.51  19.14

Columns: rowid, spray, estimate, p.value, s.value, conf.low, conf.high, rowid_dedup 
Type:  invlink(link) 
```


:::
:::



Rate ratios relative to spray A:



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
avg_comparisons(m_pois, variables = list(spray = "reference"), comparison = "ratio")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

  Term Contrast Estimate Std. Error    z Pr(>|z|)    S  2.5 % 97.5 %
 spray    B / A    1.057     0.1118 9.46   <0.001 68.1 0.8383  1.277
 spray    C / A    0.144     0.0307 4.68   <0.001 18.4 0.0834  0.204
 spray    D / A    0.339     0.0511 6.64   <0.001 34.9 0.2390  0.439
 spray    E / A    0.241     0.0415 5.82   <0.001 27.3 0.1600  0.323
 spray    F / A    1.149     0.1192 9.65   <0.001 70.7 0.9159  1.383

Columns: term, contrast, estimate, std.error, statistic, p.value, s.value, conf.low, conf.high 
Type:  response 
```


:::
:::



Check for overdispersion: residual deviance should be close to its degrees of freedom.



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
deviance(m_pois) / df.residual(m_pois)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] 1.489828
```


:::
:::



## Chi-square as a linear model

A hand-built 2×2 table: germination (yes/no) with and without cold stratification.



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
germ <- data.frame(
  treatment = rep(c("Stratified", "Control"), each = 2),
  germinated = rep(c("Yes", "No"), times = 2),
  n = c(30, 10, 18, 22)
)
xtabs(n ~ treatment + germinated, germ)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
            germinated
treatment    No Yes
  Control    22  18
  Stratified 10  30
```


:::
:::

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
chisq.test(xtabs(n ~ treatment + germinated, germ), correct = FALSE)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

	Pearson's Chi-squared test

data:  xtabs(n ~ treatment + germinated, germ)
X-squared = 7.5, df = 1, p-value = 0.00617
```


:::
:::



The same test as a Poisson regression. The **interaction** asks whether the germination split depends on treatment:



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
m_chi <- glm(n ~ treatment * germinated, family = poisson, data = germ)
anova(m_chi, test = "Rao")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
Analysis of Deviance Table

Model: poisson, link: log

Response: n

Terms added sequentially (first to last)

                     Df Deviance Resid. Df Resid. Dev    Rao Pr(>Chi)   
NULL                                     3     10.866                   
treatment             1   0.0000         2     10.866 0.0000  1.00000   
germinated            1   3.2217         1      7.644 3.2002  0.07363 . 
treatment:germinated  1   7.6440         0      0.000 7.5000  0.00617 **
---
Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
```


:::
:::



The `Rao` score statistic for the interaction matches the chi-square.

::: callout-note
## Exercise 2

Convert the same table to individual-level data (one row per seed) and fit `glm(germinated ~ treatment, family = binomial)`. Use `avg_comparisons()` to report the difference in germination probability. How does the answer relate to the chi-square result?
:::
